Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the budgetary numbers I promised we’d follow up with so you have something to share internally. I’ve attached a lightweight workbook (starchain_redwood_estimate_v3.xlsx) and a CSV export of the pricing calculator.

Call highlights (TL;DR):
- Production use case: customer support summarization + reranking for top-3 answers; estimated average context window ≈ 1.8k tokens, ~6 reqs/sec for pilot.
- Primary constraints: target latency < 350ms p95; data retention: 30 days for logs; SOC2 and IP questions to legal (Kelsey looped).
- Initial rollout: 100k monthly active users (MAU) -> estimated 350M tokens/month in month 1 pilot assumption.

Budgetary estimate (ballpark ranges, per our call):
- Model variants we discussed: latency-optimized v1 (512-1k seq), balanced v2 (1k-2k), high-throughput v3 (quantized, lower perf).
- Unit rate guidance (per 1M tokens, USD):
  - v1 (latency-optimized): $1,150 / 1M tokens
  - v2 (balanced): $750 / 1M tokens
  - v3 (quantized throughput): $420 / 1M tokens

Cost slices for your pilot (350M tokens/month):
- If using v2 mix (80% v2, 20% v3) -> blended ≈ $720 / 1M -> monthly ≈ $252,000
- If using v1 for stricter latency (50% v1, 50% v2) -> blended ≈ $952 / 1M -> monthly ≈ $333,200

Discounting and procurement notes:
- These figures are budgetary and assume a 12-month committed pilot with staged ramp; committed minimums materially reduce unit rates.
- We typically layer a 10-20% volume discount once monthly token usage crosses 1B tokens or under a 12mo reserved capacity contract.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review attached estimate — I put three volume bands (pilot 350M, scale 1B, steady-state 3B) so leadership can see unit economics at each tier.
2) Tell us target latency SLO for the feature (p50/p95) so we can recommend an exact model mapping.
3) If procurement wants a PO path, Marissa will share our standard SOW + draft terms.

I’m available for a 30-min follow-up on Wednesday if you want us to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Rishi

1) Pilot token mix: the 350M number assumes 60% summarization (short responses avg 600 tokens), 40% reranking/embedding calls (avg 300 tokens but many small calls). Does your calc treat reranking as separate embedding/queries costs?
2) Budget range: our initial procurement box is $200k - $300k / month for a 3-month pilot; if numbers are outside that we need to propose a narrower scope or hybrid architecture.
3) SLA/latency: we need p95 < 350ms — that was non-negotiable.

Can you confirm whether the blended $720/1M example for v2 mix could be brought to $600/1M under a 3mo committed pilot with a short-term reserved pool? Also please confirm whether the pricing workbook shows token definitions (input vs output) — we want to map to our ingestion side correctly.

1) Reranking/embedding: treated separately in the sheet. Embedding/rerank ops are priced as lower-per-token math in the calc sheet because typical vector requests are smaller; I left an assumptions table that splits the pilot traffic into: 60% summarization (input + output tokens counted together in generation pricing), 30% rerank queries (smaller generation + embedding calls), 10% embeddings-only batches.

2) Budget band: For a 3-month committed pilot with short-term reserved pool (min commit 350M/mo, billed monthly) we can improve the blended v2 band to $600 / 1M tokens blended. I put this as a commitment-tier line in the workbook ("3mo reserved - pilot"). That would put the pilot at ~ $210,000 / month for your 350M example.

3) Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms is achievable on our balanced v2 with a colocated dedicated pool and conservative batching (we'll size for 6 req/s with headroom). Dev is copied to scope the infra configuration that meets that SLO. For safety, we recommend a canary with v2 for the first 2 weeks and fallback rules to v3 if throughput spikes.

Attachments included in this email: starchain_redwood_estimate_v3.xlsx (updated with input/output token rows), pricing_calc_v3.csv.
